claim: Modena Cathedral, Torre Civica (Ghirlandina) and Piazza Grande were inscribed together as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997 as a Romanesque masterpiece created jointly by architect Lanfranco and sculptor Wiligelmo.
quote: Cathedral, Torre Civica and Piazza Grande, Modena... The Cathedral... is a supreme example of early Romanesque art. The work of two great artists (Lanfranco and Wiligelmus)...

claim: The official Modena UNESCO site description groups the Cathedral, Ghirlandina Tower and Piazza Grande, plus the Palazzo Comunale and the communal Acetaia, with reservation required for some access.
quote: access to some locations within the UNESCO Site of Modena is available by reservation only

claim: Inside the Duomo, visitors see Wiligelmo's Genesis reliefs and the Porta Regia rose window, the Campionesi-carved Pontile (rood screen) with Passion scenes above the raised chancel, and the crypt with the tomb of San Geminiano on 11th-century Lombard columns.
quote: Pontile... with scenes from the Passion... Sepolcro di San Geminiano... in the central apse of the crypt... three naves supported by 11th-century Lombard columns

claim: Wiligelmo's four marble Genesis panels on the Duomo's west façade (c. 1099–1110) — Creation, Adam and Eve, Cain and Abel, Noah's Ark — are considered the fountainhead of Romanesque sculpture in northern Italy and a likely model for Saint-Denis near Paris.
quote: his figures are squat and full of earthy vigour... was the fountainhead of Romanesque sculpture in northern Italy

claim: The Duomo's north portal, Porta della Pescheria, carries one of the earliest known monumental depictions of the King Arthur legend (the 'Modena Archivolt'), carved c. 1120–1140 — decades before Geoffrey of Monmouth and Chrétien de Troyes popularised the cycle.
quote: Decorated with high relief carvings of secular scenes from the Breton tales of King Arthur, these 'Modena Archivolt' reliefs are one of the earliest depictions of the theme

claim: The Ghirlandina (about 86 m tall, ~200 steps) is climbed by timed reservation only, in groups of up to 25, with entry slots roughly every 45 minutes from 9:45 to 18:00 daily; reduced ticket is €4 and free for under-12s.
quote: Access is by reservation only and limited to groups of up to 25 people per time slot

claim: Building of the Duomo began in 1099 and the Ghirlandina was completed in 1319; the cathedral itself is free and open 07:00–19:00, with the Musei del Duomo (lapidarium and tapestries) charging €6 and closed Mondays.
quote: Cathedral: Free entry, open 7:00–19:00 daily... Museum: €6.00; hours 10:00–14:00 and 15:00–18:00 (Tue–Fri)... closed Mondays

claim: The Galleria Estense occupies the top floor of the Palazzo dei Musei across four halls and sixteen rooms, with set-piece masterworks including Bernini's marble bust of Francesco I d'Este, Velázquez's portrait of the same duke, El Greco's Modena Triptych, Correggio's Madonna and Child, and Cima da Conegliano's Pietà.
quote: four large halls and sixteen rooms... Bernini's marble Bust of Francesco I d'Este... El Greco's Modena Triptych

claim: Galleria Estense holds a 4.5/5 rating on TripAdvisor (#7 of 228 Modena attractions) with reviewers calling it 'world class' and singling out the Bernini Francesco I bust as the showstopper; ticket €8, closed Mondays.
quote: Bernini's marble bust of Francesco I d'Este (mentioned repeatedly as a showstopper)... 'a wonderful collection, superbly curated with excellent information in English'

claim: The Biblioteca Estense Universitaria, also inside Palazzo dei Musei, is free to enter Mon–Thu 08:30–19:00, Fri to 15:30 and Sat to 13:30; its centrepiece is the 15th-century Bibbia di Borso d'Este, a two-volume Latin Bible with over 1,000 illuminated miniatures of the Ferrara school.
quote: Borso d'Este Bible... two-volume Latin Bible... over 1,200 pages and more than 1,000 miniatures

claim: Lonely Planet's listing flags the Biblioteca Estense's Borso d'Este Bible as the must-see, noting the original is glass-cased while a high-quality facsimile is available for visitors to leaf through.
quote: The centrepiece is the Bible that belonged to Borso d'Este, a 15th-century masterwork of illuminated miniature of the Ferrara School... The original is encased in glass, but there is a replica for you to peruse

claim: The Museo Civico (also in Palazzo dei Musei) was founded in 1871 and splits into a Medieval/Modern Art wing and an Archaeological-Ethnological wing; highlights include Begarelli's terracotta Madonna di Piazza, the nationally important 'terramare' Bronze Age collection, Etruscan and Roman finds, and Lamberto Loria's New Guinea ethnography.
quote: Madonna di piazza, a wonderful terracotta statue by the Modenese Antonio Begarelli (1499-1565)... The 'terramare' collection is one of the most important at the national level

claim: Palazzo Ducale, the 1634 Este residence on Piazza Roma, now houses Italy's Military Academy and can only be visited by guided tour on Saturdays and Sundays (≈1 hour inside), booked by the Wednesday before with ID details; standard ticket €10.
quote: The palace can be visited only with a guided tour on Saturdays and Sundays upon reservation... Reservations are required by Wednesday before the visit

claim: The Palazzo Ducale tour covers the State Apartment with the recently reopened Salone d'Onore (Hall of Honor) plus the Military Academy's museum rooms, telling the Este dynasty story from Ferrara exile to 19th-century Modena rule.
quote: the museum rooms of the Military Academy and the rooms of the State Apartment where you can admire the magnificent Hall of Honor recently reopened

claim: Teatro Comunale Pavarotti-Freni runs guided 'behind-the-scenes' tours covering foyer, stalls, stage, ridotto and normally-closed tailoring and set-design workshops; it was renamed in 2007 for Pavarotti and re-named again in October 2021 to add Mirella Freni after her death.
quote: Since October 2021, following the death of the Modena soprano, the Theatre has been entitled 'Teatro Comunale Pavarotti-Freni'

claim: The neoclassical Teatro Comunale was designed by Francesco Vandelli and inaugurated on 3 October 1841 with Gandini's opera 'Adelaide di Borgogna al Castello di Canossa'; its core structure is unchanged and it is tied to Modena-born singers Pavarotti, Freni, Kabaivanska and Ghiaurov.
quote: The new theater was inaugurated on the evening of October 3rd 1841, with the opera 'Adelaide of Borgogna at the Canossa Castle' with music by Alessandro Gandini

claim: Modena's Synagogue on Piazza Mazzini, completed 1873 to plans by Ludovico Maglietta, is one of the largest in Italy and stands at the heart of the former Jewish ghetto, with a deep-blue dome painted with gold stars; visits are by advance booking Mon–Thu 09:00–12:30 only, closed for Jewish holidays and the last three weeks of August.
quote: The temple was completed in 1873, to plans drawn up by Ludovico Maglietta... The domed ceiling is painted a vibrant blue with a sprinkling of golden stars throughout

claim: Modena was historically a major centre of Jewish culture under Este protection, especially renowned for kabbalistic scholarship, which is the cultural backdrop to today's synagogue visit.
quote: Modena was a centre of Jewish life and culture, with Jews protected by the Este dynasty and flourishing in the fields of scholarship and kabbalistic study

claim: Modena's own one-day itinerary prioritises Piazza Grande and the UNESCO trio in the morning, lunch at the Albinelli market, then Palazzo dei Musei (Galleria Estense) and Palazzo Ducale in the afternoon — pointedly omitting the Biblioteca Estense and Synagogue.
quote: The only place to start your tour is the beautiful Piazza Grande, which has always been the heart of the city

claim: Piazza Grande has been the civic-religious heart of Modena since the burial of patron saint Geminiano in 397, fronted by both the Duomo and the Palazzo Comunale (town hall), and is where the free Comune was founded and historic events including public executions took place.
quote: the place where the religious and civil power meet (the Palazzo Comunale - Town Hall - is also here). All the historic events of Modena took place here, from the burial of the Patron Saint Geminiano in 397
